outcome: Length of stay after cesarean deliveries
Length of stay after vaginal deliveries
cohort: Obese pregnant women (n=1,048,323) from the Nationwide Inpatient Sample database (2010-2014)
finding: Obese pregnant women had a significantly greater risk for adverse obstetrical outcomes, leading to increased hospital and economic burden.
mod_finding: Obese women were more likely to have cesarean deliveries (aOR 1.70, 95% CI 1.62-1.79) and labor inductions (aOR 1.51, 95% CI 1.42-1.60), and experience greater length of stay after both cesarean deliveries (aOR 1.14, 95% CI 1.08-1.36) and vaginal deliveries (aOR 1.48, 95% CI 1.23-1.77).
